sentences.text:
Appearance:
 Shri Sudhir Dandwate - Advocate for the appellant.
 Shri Akhil Godha - Advocate for respondents no.1 and 2  ORDER

This Misc. Appeal under Section 173(1) of the Motor Vehicles Act, 1988 has been filed by the appellant/Insurance Company assailing the impugned award dated 27.04.2017 passed by III Member Motor Accident Claims Tribunal, Shajapur (M.P.) in Claim Case No.54/2015, whereby an amount of Rs.41,19,859/- has been awarded to the survivors of the deceased Shivnarayan Altoliya along with interest.

entities.text: III Member Motor Accident Claims Tribunal, Shajapur
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: 2. It is not in dispute that the deceased Shivnarayan Altoliya died due to injuries suffered in a road traffic accident occurred on 05.03.2015.
3. Learned counsel for the Insurance Company submits that this is case where FIR Ex.P-2 was lodged against unknown vehicle.

Nothing was mentioned in the FIR that any one has witnessed the accident, but after near about a week, in collusion with the owner of the offending vehicle Tavera bearing registration no.MP-42-BC-0571, witness Jagdish (PW-2) was implanted as eye witness and his statement under Section 161 of Cr.P.C was recorded and thereafter charge sheet was filed against the driver/respondent no.3 stating that Tavera bearing NEUTRAL CITATION NO.
2026:MPHC-IND:8702 2 MA-1224-2017 registration no.MP-42-BC-0571 was rashly and negligently driven by respondent no.3 has caused the accident.
He further submits that it is a case of false involvement of the vehicle for grabbing the compensation amount.
To buttress his submission he has read out the statement of Jagdish (PW-2).
On these submissions learned counsel prays for allowing the appeal by setting aside the impugned award.

4. Per contra , learned counsel for the claimants submits that even though FIR Ex.P-2 was lodged against unknown vehicle, but during the course of investigation, by the statement of Jagdish (PW-2)
it transpires that the aforementioned Tavera bearing registration no.MP-42-BC-0571 was rashly and National Insurance Co. Ltd. vs Smt. Gangabai on 2 April, 2026 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/67475486/
1 negligently driven by respondent no.3 resulting in the accident wherein deceased Shivnarayan Altoliya suffered grievous injuries and passed away.

sentences.text: He further submits that Claims Tribunal has taken into account the evidence available on record coupled with the fact that no evidence in rebuttal has been adduced by the Insurance Company.

On these contentions he submits that no illegality or irregularity has been committed by the learned Claims Tribunal in holding the Insurance Company responsible for payment of the compensation amount.
Hence, urges the Court for dismissing the appeal filed by the Insurance Company.

To buttress his submissions, he has placed reliance on the order dated 21.01.2026 in M.A.No.2153/2013 (Legal Manager IFFCOTOKIO General Insurance Company Limited Vs. Smt. Krishna Kunwar and others) and another connected matter and also order dated 22.12.2023 in M.A.No.2853/2008 (United Insurance Co.Ltd.through Legal Cell Vs. Raksingh Bhilala and others).
5.

sentences.text: Heard and considered the submissions of the learned counsel for the parties and perused the record.
NEUTRAL CITATION NO. 2026:MPHC-IND:8702 3 MA-1224-2017 6.

It is not in dispute that FIR Ex.P-2 has been lodged against unknown vehicle and deceased Shivnarayan Altoliya was found lying on the road with bleeding injuries and he succumbed to the injuries on the spot.
FIR was lodged on the same day.

Ultimately after investigation, Tavera bearing registration no.MP- 42-BC-0571 was seized and the driver/respondent no.3 was arrested and on completion of investigation, charge sheet has been filed against the aforesaid driver under Section 304-A of IPC.
6.1 From perusal of the record, it is apparent that Jagdish (PW-2) has been examined as eye witness.

Even though certain infirmities have been found in his statement, but the infirmities are not so fatal to the claimants' case and coupled with the fact that neither Insurance Company has adduced any evidence in rebuttal nor investigating officer has been examined who could have thrown some light that the offending vehicle was involved in the accident.
7. In the aforesaid circumstances, it cannot be said in the teeth of evidence available on record that the award passed by the Claims Tribunal is perverse.
Resultantly, the appeal filed by the Insurance Company is devoid of substance, fails and is hereby dismissed.

(BINOD KUMAR DWIVEDI) JUDGE RJ National Insurance Co. Ltd. vs Smt. Gangabai on 2 April, 2026 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/67475486/
